Scope of Credit Transfer
Students can apply for up to 20 credits per semester to be transferred as liberal arts or major credits.
Students can apply for up to 1/2 of their credits required for graduation recognized from their studies abroad
Credits from studying abroad can be transferred up to 1/2 of credits required for graduation.
Can be transferred as major credits (core or advanced major), liberal arts credits, and general elective credits
Before Departure
Before departure, students must decide on the courses they plan to take at the hosting university and check with their home university's administrative team whether the courses can be transferred for credit.
As for minors and multiple majors, students must check in advance whether credits can be transferred by the relevant college at Hanyang University.
After Returning Home
Step 1 [Office of International Affairs]: School registration transfer and credit transfer procedures Returning students must complete their Return Report on the HY-in system (Student HY-in > Application > Credit Exchange Management > Exchange & Study Abroad > Exchange Study Abroad Application History menu)
Step 2 [[Student]]: Upload the Return Report to HY-in Before the end of the Exchange/study abroad Program, students must read the Credit Transfer Procedure sent to their private e-mail account and enter all relevant coursework (information of the semester completed, courses taken (English), credits earned for each subject, grade) completed at the hosting university directly on the HY-in system (directory: Student HY-in - Application - Academic Grades - Hosting University Credit Transfer Application menu) (1) What if the hosting university does note grade students on an alphabetical grading system (e.g. ABCDF)? If the hosting university has a conversion table, use it to convert your academic grades. In the absence of such a table, use the “Academic Grade Conversion Table by Country (Europe)” sent via e-mail from the Office of International Affairs. (2) Do not alter ECTS information arbitrarily (e.g. Multiplying 2/3) Students must enter the ECTS on their transcript into the system as is, and the credits will be corrected and entered into the system once their college administrator reviews the credits. (3) What if a student receives an “F” grade or drops out of a course? Enter information as it appears on the academic transcript. ※ Caution Course names must be entered in English, and all credits or grades must be entered exactly as they appear on the transcript. If you discover an error that requires editing after submitting or printing documents, contact the administrative department at your college and ask them to activate the Edit function in the Credit Transfer Application Menu. Once you click to save drafts, the system will register any input information or documents. Exercise caution when submitting all documents.
Step 3 [[Student]]: Submit materials for credit transfer review (1) Print out the Statement of Exchange Student Course Completion Upon entering academic grades in the HY-in system, click the <Print> button at the top of the screen to print. ※ Students enrolled in multiple majors/minors: Print out the Statement of Exchange Student Course Completion for each major/minor. (2) Submit the Statement for main major and other majors/minors to the administrative department. (By major) Statement of Exchange Student Course Completion + Academic Transcript from the hosting university + Course Outline (English/Korean) ※ Caution Only courses that have been reviewed for credit transfer in the main major in advance can be reviewed for transfer as a multiple major/minor credit. Please note that review for major courses is required even for classes unrelated to the major.
Step 4 [[College/Department]: The student’s department reviews academic performance, and sends results to the Academic Affairs Team. ※ Grades for each course completed overseas are ultimately reviewed and converted to P/F by the student’s department.
Step 5 [Academic Affairs Team]: Academic Affairs Team confirms the final grades. ※ If you discover an error that requires editing after submitting or printing documents, contact the Administrative Department at your college and ask them to activate the Edit function in the Credit Transfer Application Menu (OIA does not have the authority to edit any information input by the student).

Greetings from the World Smart Sustainable Cities Organization (WeGO).
WeGO Smart City Champions
(Application Deadline 2 March 2022)
We are delighted to inform you that WeGO will organize the WeGO Smart City Champions , a youth program which will recruit youth from universities in member cities from all around the world to gain knowledge and build consensus around the future of smart cities. By fostering knowledge exchange and building capacities of youth in the field of urban development, sustainability and smart cities, this flagship program will empower young urban leaders of tomorrow to build safe and inclusive smart cities.
Through two phases, Phase I: Smart City Conceptual Foundation (lectures), and Phase II: Smart City Capacity Building (workshops), the program will guide and provide insight to the participants in exploring innovative solutions to current smart city challenges.
More specifically, the lectures of Phase I aim to equip participants with the conceptual knowledge of smart cities. Through these lectures, participants will have a greater understanding of current smart city challenges and solutions. It will provide an opportunity for participants to learn from key experts and representatives from renowned corporations and institutions in the field of smart city development.
If you are interested in participating, please fill out the application form by 2 March 2022 .
The Smart City Champions is open to all individuals under 35.
All participants of Phase I and Phase II will receive WeGO Champions Certificate and the selected winners will receive an award presented by the President of WeGO (Mayor of Seoul Metropolitan Government), in addition to prize money (maximum 300만원).
For more details, please refer to the attached files.

Attachment: [Concept Note]
WeGO Smart City Champions
About
WeGO recruits youth from universities in member cities from all around the world to gainknowledge and build consensus around the future of smart cities. By fostering knowledgeexchange and building capacities of youth in the field of urban development, sustainability andsmart cities, this flagship program will empower young urban leaders of tomorrow.
Programme OverviewTheme: Empowering Young Urban Leaders of Tomorrow to Build Safe and Inclusive Smart Cities
Goal: Fostering knowledge and building capacities in youth in Korea and overseas in the field ofurban development, sustainability and smart cities.
Eligibility:
● Open to all youth under 35
Objective:
● Facilitate active engagement of youth from Korea and overseas in the discussion ofempowerment of youth as future leaders;
● Provide a space for discussion on the importance of young people and formulaterecommendations to advance the youth development agenda for potential inclusion inkey processes and frameworks surrounding smart city development;
● Build the capacity of, and support, youth to engage in shaping the direction of smartcities;
● Foster interaction and networking opportunities among youth and other relevantstakeholders through workshops; and
● Establish partnerships with domestic and international universities and include them inthe WeGO network.
Registration
● Submit application form by March 2, 2022 (Wed).
Platform for the Program
● Phase 1: Google Classroom
● Phase 2: Zoom
Detailed Program
Youth participants are invited to partake in two phases over the course of 15 weeks.
The program will begin in early March and will end in June.
Through two phases, Phase I: Smart City Conceptual Foundation, and Phase II: Smart CityCapacity Building, the program will guide and provide insight to the participants in exploringinnovative solutions to current smart city challenges.
All participants of Phase I and Phase II will receive WeGO Champions Certificate and theselected winners will receive an award presented by the President of WeGO (Mayor of SeoulMetropolitan Government).
WeGO will fully support youth participants and will provide necessary resources throughout theprogram.
● Phase I: Smart City Conceptual Foundation (8 weeks)
○ Duration: March 4 - April 24, 2022 (6 lectures)
○ Platform: Google Classroom
○ Format: 50 minutes (Pre-recorded videos)
■ Over the course of 6 weeks, a pre-recorded lecture will be uploaded everyMonday morning at 9:00 am (Seoul, GMT+9).
○ Attendance: A quiz will be simultaneously uploaded with the respectivepre-recorded lecture, which will evaluate the participant’s attendance andunderstanding of the course material.
■ Over the course of 6 weeks, participants are required to submit thecompleted quiz by every Sunday evening at 11:59 pm (Seoul, GMT+9).
○ Objective: The lectures aim to equip participants with the conceptual knowledgeof smart cities. Through these lectures, participants will have a greaterunderstanding of current smart city challenges and solutions. It will provide anopportunity for participants to learn from key experts and representatives fromrenowned corporations and institutions in the field of smart city development.
Phase IWeek Conceptual Foundation
Week 1 Orientation Day
(March 4)
Week 2(March 7-13) Introduction to Smart City & SDGs (11)
Week 3(March 14-20) Emerging Smart Technologies and Leveraging Open Data
Week 4(March 21-27) Emerging Challenges of Digitalization, Globalization, and Urbanization
Week 5(March 28-April 3) Cybersecurity Threats in the Age of Rapid Digitalization
Week 6(April 4-10) Urban Retrofitting for Greater Resilience: Nature Based Solutions
Week 7(April 11-17) Ethics of Data Management in Smart Cities
Week 8(April 18-24) Break
● Phase II Smart City Capacity Building (7 weeks)
○ Duration: April 25 - June 12, 2022
○ Platform: Zoom
○ Application: Upon the successful completion of Phase I: Smart City ConceptualFoundation, participants are highly encouraged to formulate teams amongthemselves and submit a project plan, which will outline clear steps, methods,stakeholders and solutions to solving a pressing smart city challenge. Participantswill have two weeks to prepare for the project plan, starting from Phase II. Thedeadline to submit the project plan is May 8, 2022 (Sun).
■ One team should consist of at least 5 participants.
○ Format: 60 minutes (Online workshops)
■ Over the course of 7 weeks, a capacity building workshop will be openedonce a week from Week 3 for participants to:
● Share progress of developing their project proposals
● Exchange key know-hows to resolving challenges
● Network with other youth participants
● Learn from the lessons of experts and receive overall guidance
● Conduct student-led lectures
■ The capacity building workshop will open every week on Friday morningat 10:00 am (Seoul, GMT+9).
○ Objective:
■ The capacity building workshops aim to provide a platform for discussionand interaction among youth participants. Through the workshops,participants will have the opportunity to incubate their ideas andconstruct innovative solutions to solve a crucial challenge. The workshopwill also strengthen team building skills of participants as they willcollaboratively work together over the course of 7 weeks in preparationfor a final presentation.
○ Resources:
■ WeGO will provide necessary resources and access to its network tosupport participants in strengthening their project proposals and inimplementing their ideas.
■ WeGO will assist in guiding youth participants in preparing for the finalpresentation, which should consist of key solutions to smart citychallenges discussed during the lectures.
○ Semi-Finals:
■ During the 6th week, all teams will convene to conduct a rehearsal oftheir presentations.
■ Upon the evaluation of the rehearsals, 10 teams will be selected toproceed to the Finals.
○ Finals:
■ During the final week, selected teams will convene to present theirsolutions that have been developed during Phase II and upgraded uponfeedback from the Semi-Finals.
■ The final presentation will reflect the team’s understanding of the theme,planning of the project, and execution of their proposed solutions.
■ After an evaluation process conducted by the judging panel, the top 3teams will be awarded the following:
● 1st place: KRW 3,000,000
● 2nd place: KRW 2,000,000
● 3rd place: KRW 1,000,000
■ The three winners will also be awarded a Mayoral Award, signed by thePresident of WeGO (Mayor of Seoul Metropolitan Government).
Phase IIWeek Capacity Building & Team Building Workshop
Week 1(April 25-May 1) Formulation of TeamsProject Plan Preparation
Week 2(May 2-8) Project Plan Preparation and Submission (May 8)
Week 3(May 9-15) Design Thinking Process and Methodology
Week 4(May 16-22) Expert-led Mentorship and Guidance
Week 5(May 23-29) Student-led Lectures
Week 6(May 30-June 5) Semi-Finals: Rehearsal of Presentations and Feedback Exchange(teams will be selected to proceed to the finals)
Week 7(June 6-12) Finals: Group Presentation Day
Awards and Certificates
● Upon successful completion of Phase I and Phase II, participants will receive a WeGOChampions Certificate, which will be valuable proof of acquiring in-depth knowledge onsmart cities.
● WeGO Champions selected winners will receive:
○ Mayoral Award, signed by the President of WeGO (Mayor of Seoul MetropolitanGovernment).
○ Prize money
○ The opportunity to meet with high-level leaders and experts.
○ The chance to present at the Seoul Smart City Leaders Forum, organized by theSeoul Metropolitan Government.
○ An invitation to the WeGO Year-end Ceremony to congratulate them on theirachievements throughout the year and will have the opportunity to present theirwork to the key figures including world mayors, ambassadors, CEOs andesteemed professors.

△ You may experience pain, swelling, or redness in your injection area . You may experience fatigue,

△ You may experience a severe allergic reaction with symptoms such as breathing difficulty and swelling
of the face, eyes, lips, or inside of the mouth.
△ You may feel pain, tightness, or discomfort in the chest. You may experience breathing difficulty or
pain while breathing.
△ You may feel out of breath or experience heart palpitations. You may feel dizzy or lose consciousness.
Handling Adverse Reactions to COVID-19 Vaccination
△ If you have swelling or pain in your injection area, place a clean, dry towel over the area and massage
with ice.
△ If you have a mild fever, drink plenty of water and rest.
△ Take paracetamol to treat fever or muscular pain.
△ See a doctor if you experience any of the following issues.
- Recurrence or worsening of pain, tightness, or discomfort in the chest, breathing difficulty, shortness
of breath, or pain while breathing, heart palpitations, feeling dizziness, or loss of consciousness.
- Pain, swelling, or redness in your injection area or fever that does not subside after two days.
- A sudden loss of energy or symptoms previously not experienced.
△ If you experience severe breathing difficulty, nausea, swelling of the face, or hives, call 119 or get to
the nearest emergency room.

The Institute of Euro-African Studies (IEAS) ( http://africa.hanyang.ac.kr/ ) is offering foreign graduate students enrolled in the Department of Political Science and International Studies an opportunity to apply for the IEAS fellowship program. Please kindly refer to the details below:
[Selection criteria]
- Only enrolled freshman of post graduate students in the Department of Political Science and International Studies at Hanyang University are eligible to apply for this scholarship
- Scholarship is awarded to 1 (one) student each semester
- Although the opportunity is open to all postgraduate students, the IEAS Scholarship was developed to encourage enrolled students from either least developed countries (LDCs) or less economically developed countries.
- Second priority shall be given to the students from multicultural families in South Korea.
- Students whose research areas are related to the studies that IEAS conducts will be also given an advantage
[Requirements]
- Scholarship recipients must achieve a certain level of academic score each semester in order to retain their scholarship.
- Scholarship recipients must write: (1) a letter of appreciation to the donors; and, (2) a final activity report before graduation.
Application method: Applicants shall submit their documents every semester.
For application and inquiries please contact us: [email]

4. ELIGIBILITY
■ Eligibility
◈ Nationality
○ All applicants must hold citizenship of NIIED designated countries that are invited to take
part in the GKS program
 Applicants’ parents (or legal guardians) must hold citizenship from another
country other than Korea. If applicants or their parent hold dual citizenship (one
who has both Korean citizenship and citizenship of another country), such
applicant is NOT eligible to apply
 Applicants and their parents who had previously held Korean citizenship must
submit documentation issued by the Korean government that proves their
renunciation of Korean citizenship
 If an applicant’s citizenship is changed during the selection process, he or she
will be excluded from the evaluation. (Not applicable to International
Organization program)
※ Applicants from all countries around the world can apply to International Organization program
◈ Level of Education
○ All applicants must have obtained the required degree (as specified below) or must be
expected to graduate by July 31, 2026
Program Minimum Level
of Education
Notes
Degree
Master’s Bachelor’s Degree -

Research

Exchange Professor Master’s Degree Must be a current academic professor
Professional Master’s Degree Must be a professional in a field of Education, Science, Culture, or International Cooperation
- Applicants who are expected to graduate by July 31, 2026 can also apply for the program with a certificate
of expected graduation and grades for all completed semesters at the time of application. Such

GKS Center, NIIED by July 31, 2026. Failure to do so will result in the cancellation of your acceptance.
13
◈ Grades
○ Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of the entire curriculum from the previous degree
program* must meet one of the conditions below;
* For example, previous degree for a doctoral degree program applicant is a master’s degree program
 Score percentile should be 80% or above on a 100 -point scale or be ranked in the top
20% of one’s class
 CGPA must be equal to or above 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4. 3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0
 Applicants must submit an academic transcript with CGPA or ranking
information
 If a transcript does not provide CGPA in any one of the accepted GPA scales
(4.0, 4.3, 4.5, 5.0 or 100 point scale), then the applicant must submit a transcript
converted into one of the above GPA scales as a supplementary document
 Applicants who are expec ted to graduate must submit their grades for all
completed semesters at the time of application
◈ Age
○ Must be under 40 years of age (born after September 1, 1986)
○ Current a cademic professors in one of the Official Development Assistance (ODA)
recipients* who are under 45 years of age (born after September 1, 1981) are eligible to apply.
* DAC List of ODA Recipients on 202 5 flows ( www.oecd.org )
◈ Language ability
○ Applicants who are expected to complete the IRTS Korean language program by August
2026 are eligible to apply if they have achieved a TOPIK, TOPIK IBT Level 3 or higher.
* Accepted certificates include TOPIK results from the 93rd to the 105th exams and TOPIK IBT
results from the 1st to the 12th exams. (Applicants who have not yet obtained a valid TOPIK
certificate at the time of application may still apply.)
◈ Health
○ All applicants must be in good health, both mentally and physically, to study in Korea for
the full duration of the program.

■ Restriction
◈ A person who has graduated (or is expected to graduate) from a
Korean high school (including international school s in Korea ) or a
Korean u niversity * is NOT eligible to apply
* In accordance with Article 29 of the Higher Education Act, both undergraduate and graduate
programs are included.
 A person who has graduated from an online curriculum from a Korean high school
or a Korean university cannot apply
 A person who is currently in his/her final year at a Korean university cannot apply
◈ A person who has previously received a scholarship from the
Korean government is NOT eligible to apply
○ A person who had previously enrolled at a degree program through a Korean government
sponsored scholarship program other than the NIIED administered scholarship program
cannot apply
○ A GKS scholar whose scholarship was canceled after beginning a degree program
(including the one-year Korean language course) or the IRTS Korean language program
○ A former GKS scholar who had enrolled in a degree or research program
 ‘Cancellation of Scholarship’ means a GKS scholar either withdrew from the
program or his/her scholarship was forfeited due to cumulative warnings, etc.
during their scholarship period
 A former GKS scholar who ha d received scholarships from GKS Non -degree
program for exchange students and IRTS Korean language program CAN apply
◈ Final successful candidates of the GKS degree program from the past
three years who have withdrawn from the program or was disqualified
from the program prior to enrollment cannot apply
◈ Duplicate Submission
○ Embassy track candidates (including reserve candidates) who passed the first round of
selection cannot apply again through a university track
○ Embassy track applicants must apply to only ONE program among General, and Overseas
Korean/ Adoptee program

○ University track applicants must apply to only ONE program among General, R -GKS,
Research, R&D or Global Network program
* However, applicants recommended by International Organization may apply to only one program
among General, R-GKS, Research, R&D, or Global Network under the University track, excluding
the research program
○ University track applicants (including a pplicants recommended by the International
Organization) must apply to ONE university and ONE department
※ Duplicate submissions are not permitted and will be excluded from the evaluation. If
identified at any stage of the selection process, the scholarship will be revoked.

APPENDIX E. 2026 GKS-G APPLICATION FAQS
Q. Should I submit my parents’ passport copy?
A. It is necessary to submit an official document (i.e., the applicant’s birth certificate or family
register) that proves you and your parents' relationship. If the document does not include you and
your parents' citizenship information, then you should submit additional documents (i.e., a passport
copy or other government -issued document that indicates citizenship information) for proof of
citizenship. Please note that birthplace or ethnic group information on a birth certificate or current
residency in the submitted documents will not be accepted as proof of citizenship.
Q. My father deceased a long time ago, and I cannot provide his proof of citizenship.
A. If you are not able to issue your parent(s)’ proof of citizenshi p due to your parent(s)’ absence
(e.g., divorced, deceased, etc.), then please provide supplementary documents that explain the
reason for not submitting their proof of citizenship. (e.g., divorce certificate or death certificate).
Q. My parents and I hold different citizenships. Am I eligible to apply for the program?
A. Yes, you may. As long as you and your parent(s) do not hold Korean citizenship, and if you
have citizenship of the country that is invited to the GKS degree program, you are eligible to apply.
54
Q. My country is not listed in the 2026 GKS-G program. Can I apply for the program?
A. The quota allocation is decided based on mutual agreements on cultural and educational
cooperation between Korea and the participating countries. All applicants must hold citizenship of
the GKS partner country except for the R&D, Global Network, and International Organization
programs. These programs are open to all countries around the world. Applicants for R&D, Global
Network, or International Organization programs must directly apply to their designated
universities since the program is only available under a university track.
Q. I am expected to graduate from my degree program in March 2026. Am I eligible to apply
for this program?
A. Yes. Applicants who are expected to graduate by July 31, 2026, can also apply for the program
with a certificate of expected graduation. Such applicants must submit their official graduation
certificate (or diploma) and final academic transcript to the GKS Center, NIIED, by July 31, 2026.
Failure to do so will result in the cancellation of your acceptance.
Q. It takes one year in my country to get a diploma after my graduation. Can I apply with
my provisional graduation certificate (or provisional degree certificate)?
A. No. Only an official (final) graduation certificate, degree certificate, or diploma is acceptable.
The graduation certificate must clearly indicate the date (or at least the month) of official
graduation. A provisional certificate is not accepted as a graduation certificate in the GKS degree
program even if it is acknowledged as an official graduation certificate in your home country.
Q. I have a master’s degree. Can I apply for a master’s degree program in a different major?
Which degree certificate should I submit?
A. You can apply for a master's program while holding another master's degree. If you are applying
to a master’s degree program, you should submit a degree certificate and academic transcript of
your bachelor's degree. In this case, your CGPA for your bachelor’s degree should meet the grade
requirement in the application guidelines. Providing your master’s degree certificate and academic
transcript is optional.
Q. I am currently in my master’s degree program at a university in Korea. Am I eligib le to
apply for the master’s degree program at another university?
A. If you have graduated from a Korean high school or a Korean university, or if you are currently
enrolled in the final year of your degree curriculum (or if you are about to obtain a degr ee) at a
Korean university, you cannot apply for the GKS degree program. If you are not near the
graduation, you may apply for the program. However, if you are selected as our GKS scholar, you
must drop out of the Korean university you are currently enrolled at and start the degree program
under GKS as a first -year. Transfer credits from your previous university will not be accepted.
Applicants currently residing in Korea may be required to return to their home country to obtain a
new visa. In such cases, the cost of entry airfare to Korea will not be provided.
56
Q. The grades in my transcript are different from the GPA scales in the guidelines. How
should I submit my CGPA? Can I use the scores I converted from a grade conversion website?
A. If your grades do not belong to any of the GPA scales we accept (4.0, 4.3, 4.5, 5.0, or 100-point
scale), you must submit a converted grade confirmed by the university. If applicants convert their
grades through a grade conversion tool such as scholaro.com, the converted CGPA must provide
official institutional proof that the converted CGPA is recognized by their university. Please submit
an official certificate or at least a testimonial issued by your university that confirms the converted
CGPA. This supplementary document does not need to be apostilled or consular confirmed but
must be submitted as an original document with the university’s authentication. The screening
committee will determine whether your CGPA is eligible for the program or not based on the
information you provide.
Q. My CGPA is below 80%. Am I still eligible to apply?
A. Yes, but only if you meet the class rank requirement. If your score percentile is below 80%,
you remain eligible only if you are ranked within the top 20% of your class. In this case, you
must submit an official certificate or a formal letter issued by your university explicitly stating
your class rank. Without this official documentation, your transcript alone will not be sufficient
for eligibility.
Q. My transcript only shows a final CGPA and does not list GPA by semester. How should I
fill out the application form?
A. If your transcript does not provide a GPA for each individual semester or year, you may leave
those specific boxes blank. However, you must provide your Final CGPA and the Score Percentile
for your entire degree. If your transcript does not show a score percentile, you must use the "GPA
Conversion Table" in the Appendix to convert your CGPA into a 100-point scale.
Q. I am applying for a doctoral degree program. Should I also submit a CGPA of my
bachelor’s degree?
A. Applicants for a doctoral degree program should put the CGPA of their previous degree
(master’s degree) on the application form. Doctoral degree program applicants should submit the
graduation certificate and official academic transcript of both bachelor’s and master’s degrees. The
CGPA required in the application is of the master’s degree.
58
Q. I am a transfer student, and my current transcript does not show the GPA from my
previous university. How should I submit my records?
A. Please submit an official academic transcript issued by the university you graduated from. If
the transcript does not in dicate your grades for the entire degree curriculum, please submit your
academic records from the previous university as a supplementary document as reference material.
The CGPA required in the application should be the one shown on the official academic transcript
from the university you have graduated from.
Q. I meet all the application requirements listed in the application guideline. Does this mean
that I am qualified to apply to all GKS partner universities?
A. Not necessarily. The application requirements we have indicated in the application guideline
are the minimum requirements to apply for the GKS program. Some universities and departments
may have additional requirements, such as a certain level of language prof iciency. Therefore, we
ask all prospective applicants to check the “University information” files posted with the
application guideline to find required qualifications set by each university/department. If a
university requests additional material (e.g., a portfolio) beyond NIIED’s required documents, you
should submit those materials directly to the university.
Q. I am currently living in Korea. Can I apply for this program?
A. Yes, you may apply for the program while residing in a different country. Applicants must
apply either through a Korean embassy where they hold citizenship (embassy track) or through a
Korean university (un iversity track). Embassy Track applicants who are applying from a third
country must check the method of application submission or interview process with the embassy.
Successful candidates who are currently residing in Korea or enter Korea from a third country will
not be provided with the entry airfare. Please be advised that obtaining mandatory authentications
such as Apostille, consular confirmation, or certified translations for documents issued abroad may
require significant time. Applicants are strong ly encouraged to prepare these documents well in
advance.
Q. Can I submit my application documents directly to NIIED?
A. No, NIIED does not accept applications directly from individual applicants. Any documents
mistakenly sent to NIIED will be excluded from the screening process and will not be returned.
Instead, you must follow the specific submission process for your chosen track.
Starting in 2026, Embassy Track applicants are required to submit their online application and all
scanned documents through the Study in Korea website (www.studyinkorea.go.kr) between 11 am
on February 12 and 6 pm on February 25 (KST). Conversely, University Track applicants cannot
use the Study in Korea website for their applications; they must submit their materials directly to
their target university according to that specific institution’s unique instructions and deadlines.
Q. When is the application deadline?
A. The deadline depends on the application track you choose.
For the Embassy Track, applications must be submitted via the Study in Korea website between
11 am on February 12 and 6 pm on February 25, 2026 (KST). Plea se note that these times are
strictly based on Seoul time.
For the university application, the submission deadline varies by university. Please contact each
university for application deadline information.
Each embassy or university has its own application submission guidelines. For inquiries related to
the application process, please contact the relevant institution.
61
Q. I am a citizen of China/ the Czech Republic. In the application guidelines, there is quota
only assigned in the embassy track for the Chinese/ the Czech citizens. Does that mean that
I must apply to the Korean Embassy in my country?
A. No. While your quota is categorized under the Embassy Track, you must submit your
application to your local government agency rather than the Korean Embassy. Based on mutual
agreements between governments, Chinese citizens must apply through the China Scholarship
Council (CSC) under the Ministry of Education in China. Similarly, Czech citizens must submit
their applications directly to the Ministry of Education of the Czech Republic. Please ensure you
follow the specific application instructions and deadlines provided by these respective national
institutions.
Q. I am a U.S. citizen living in Los Angeles. If I apply through the Embassy Track, can I
submit my application to the Korean Consulate in L.A. instead of the Korean Embassy in
Washington, D.C.?
A. Yes. Applicants from the United States and Vietnam are permitted to submit their applications
to their nearest Korean Consulate. For U.S. applicants, the Korean Embassy in Washington, D.C.,
and the Korean Consulate in Los Angeles cooperate to conduct the first round of selection.
Similarly, applicants in Vietnam may submit their documents to the Korean Embassy / Consulate
in Hanoi, Da Nang or Ho Chi Minh City.
62
Q. For the legalization on “Required certificates”, can I choose between apostille or consular
confirmation?
A. Countries that are parties to the Apostille Convention must obtain an apostille. Applicants from
countries not party to the Convention, or in cases where d ocuments cannot be apostilled, must
obtain consular confirmation from the Korean embassy or consulate in their country.
Q. Can I submit an original degree certificate and academic transcript without
apostille/consular confirmation?
A. The “Required certificates” must be submitted with an apostille or consular confirmation.
Original documents without additional authentication, notarized documents certified by only a
notary public, or certified documents confirmed by the oth er government agencies will not be
accepted. (Exception: certificate issued by Korean government or institutions should be submitted
in their original version without additional authentication.)
Q. I obtained an apostille on my graduation certificate in the past. Can I submit a copy of
this document?
A. It will not be accepted, as the document will be considered a simple photocopy. It does not
matter whether it is photocopied in color or black and white. Your document will be accepted only
if the government agency that initially issued the apostille issues a certified true copy, or if you
Q. How should I submit the documents with translation?
A. All application documents that are not written in Korean or English must be accompanied by a
certified translation. For “Required certificates,” apostille or consular confirmation is only required
either on original documents or certified translations. If the document is written in both languages
(original language and English), it does not need to be translated again.
Q. I will submit my original graduation certificate with an apostille, but it cannot be re-issued
any more. Can it be returned?
A. All application materials submitted to NIIED WILL NOT BE RETURNED UNDER ANY
CIRCUMSTANCES. Applicants are strongly advised to submit an apostilled or cons ular-
confirmed certified copy instead of the original document. If an applicant does not pass the first
round of selection, the embassy or university may or may not return the submitted documents in
accordance with its internal policy.
Please note that the graduation certificate submitted at the time of application is used only for the
selection process. Therefore, selected GKS scholars must prepare additional graduation certificates
with an apostille or consular confirmation for future procedures, such as visa application (embassy),
issuance of a standard admission letter (university), or visa status change (Korean immigration
office).
64
Q. What is the validity period of authenticated documents? Can I submit a graduation
certificate apostilled last year?
A. If an apostilled or consular confirmed document specifies an expiration date, its validity will be
determined based on that date. If no expiration date is indicated, the document will be accepted if
it is submitted within two years from the date of authentication.
Q. I have graduated from another country. Therefore, I cannot obtain an apostille on my
certificates from my government or apply for a consular confirmation from the Ko rean
embassy in my country. How should I submit my graduation certificate and academic
transcript that were issued by another country?
A. If your documents were issued from the university or from a government abroad, you should
obtain an apostille if the relevant country is a member of the Apostille Convention. If you are not
able to obtain an apostille from abroad, please check if you can obtain a consular confirmation
from the embassy/consulate of the relevant country.
Q. How many departments and universities can I apply to?
A. If you apply through the University Track, you may choose only ONE university and ONE
department.
If you apply through the Embassy Track, you may choose up to THREE universities under Type
A and Type B, and at least one of your choices must be from a Type B university.
You may select the same department for all three universities, however, you may not choose
multiple departments within a single university.
Q. Are there any tips for choosing three universities?
A. Embassy Track applicants should understand that passing the second round of selection does
not guarantee admission to the universities they have chosen. Applicants who select only highly
competitive universities may fail to receive admission from all three universities in the third round
of selection.
As each Korean university is recognized for different academic fields and has its own strengths,
applicants are advised to conduct thorough research to identify leading institutions in their intended
field of study.
Applicants should also consider that the cost of living for students at universities located in
metropolitan areas is generally higher than that of non -metropolitan universities. For reference,
GKS scholars are required to cover their accommodation expenses using the monthly stipend they
receive.
Q. Who should I obtain a letter of recommendation from?
A. We recommend you receive your recommendation letter from someo ne who can provide
thorough assessment of your academic abilities such as a professor or a dean of the department at
your previous university.
Applicants recommended by International Organizations such as the Asian Development Bank
(ADB) or the World Bank (WB) must submit a letter of recommendation issued by a partner
university, and refugee applicants must submit a letter of recommendation issue d by the United
Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
The recommendation letter must be dated within one year of the application deadline. Applicants
who have prepared their letters in advance may submit the previous year's (2025) letter of
recommendation form. While only one letter of recommendation is required, up to two may be
submitted if necessary.
Q. How do I submit a letter of recommendation through the Study in Korea website?
A. You may download the Letter of Recommendation form from the Study in Korea online
application system or use Form 5 provided in the GKS Notice on the Study in Korea website.
Applicants must obtain both the Recommender Information and the Letter of Recommendation
completed by their recommender.
67
Embassy Track applicants must scan and upload the letter to the online system. University Track
applicants must submit the letter in a sealed envelope, signed across the back flap by the
recommender, to the recommending university.
Q. Must I submit certificates of language proficiency (English or Korean)?
A. Language proficiency certificates (English: TOEFL iBT, IELTS/ Korean: TOPIK, TOPIK IBT)
are optional, and applicants may apply for GKS without them. However, some universities or
departments may require a minimum level of language proficiency. Submitting supporting
documents that demonstrate your language ability is recommended.
Proof that English was used as the medium of instruction cannot replace an official English
proficiency test certificate.
Q. Should I include a detailed research proposal in the Study Plan?
A. Yes. You must at least describe the general direction and outlines of your study plans, if not in
full detail. Please elaborate on your study objectives in Korea and tangible plans during and after
you complete the degree program.
68
Q. I am planning to apply through a university track. Can I submit my application to
multiple universities?
A. University track applicants can only apply to ONE university and ONE department. If an
applicant is found to have applied to more than two universities, his/her application document will
be excluded from the next round of evaluation. Even after the announcement of qualified applicants,
scholarships may be canceled.
Embassy track applicants whose application have not passed the first round may apply to a
university track once more. However, applicants cannot apply for both tracks at once.
Q. My name on my birth certificate is different from the one on my graduation certificate.
What should I do when the names are different on the documents?
A. Applicant must apply with the name on their passport. If the name on your passport is different
from other documents, please provide a supplementary document issued by your government that
explains the discrepancy.
Q. How will I know if I have been accepted?
A. Each embassy and university will individually announce the results of the first round of
selection. The results of the first round of selection for the Embassy Track will be announced by
March 16th. The results of the second round and the list of final successful applicants will be
announced on the Study in Korea GKS Notice Board. All important announcements for applicants
will be posted on the Study in Korea GKS notice board, so please check the board regularly during
the selection period.
Q. Is it mandatory for all GKS scholars to pass at least Level 3 in TOPIK after one year of
the Korean Language Program?
A. Yes. Every GKS scholar must achieve at least Level 3 on TOPIK (Test of Proficiency in Korean)
within a yearlong Korean language program to proceed to his or her degree program (except
scholars in a research program, global network program, IRTS Korean Language Program
graduates, current academic professors enrolled in a 100% English -taught program with the
submission of a Korean Language Exemption Application , or R&D Program applicants to 100%
English-taught program).
In addition, certain universities or departments require students to submit a valid TOPIK certificate
of level 4 or higher. Scholars who applied to such a department may not enter their degree program
if they fail to achieve the required TOPIK certificate during a yearlong Korean language program.
Q. If I become a GKS scholar, will I be assigned to a Korean language institution in a
different region of my degree university?
A. No. As of 2023, all GKS scholars will take their Korean language program at the same
university where they will conduct their degree program.
※ Exception: DGIST, KAIST, KDI School of Public Policy and Management, National Cancer
Center Graduate School of Cancer Science and Policy , POSTECH, The Academy of Korean
Studies and UNIST will designate another university for a Korean language program.
During the language program, scholars are required to live on campus. In general, scholars are
assigned to a dormitory with roommate(s). Each institution has different facilities. If a n
independent kitchen or a bathroom is mandatory for religious reasons, etc., please check with the
university of your interest.
Q. The degree program I applied to is taught in English only. May I be exempt from the
Korean Language Program?
A. A yearlong Korean language program is an important part of the GKS program. All GKS
scholars must take a Korean language program regardless of the curriculum of the degree program.
However, if you have already attained an advanced level (Level 5 or 6) on TOPIK when applying
for the program, you must submit your valid TOPIK certificate to be exempt from the Korean
language program. You will directly start your degree program in September 2026.
71

Ⅰ. Overview of the University
❍ Hanyang University, a world-class talent fosterer
Hanyang University has been producing graduates who stand out in Korea’s leading
companies and organizations such as Samsung, LG and Hyundai. Hanyang ranks 1st for
producing the most CEO’s of venture and 3rd for producing most number of alumni who
became successful CEO’s among 100 Korea’s leading companies. The university has
produced many of the world’s finest who have shape our world across all sectors,
including CEO’s of leading companies, senior government officials, and diverse influencers
in cultural and sports stars.
❍ Korea's largest educational institution and research-oriented university
Hanyang University ranks in the top in Korea with one teacher-to-student ratio per nine
students. Seoul Campus comprises a general graduate school, professional graduate school,
and specialized graduate school, offering approximately 78 departments. The University also
operates an industry-academic cooperative R&D center to solve on long-term research that is
difficult for companies to address and also operates Hospital in Seoul and Guri. Furthermore,
Hanyang is recognized as a Korea’s leading university education institution, boasting the
largest manpower, with over 36,000 students, 5,000 faculty members, and a network of
390,000 alumni.
❍ Education centered on technology start-ups
Hanyang University has been producing the most CEOs among venture companies. The
university operates a global entrepreneur center established to educate "prepared
technology entrepreneurs" and an industry-academic digital park established to promote
and support joint cooperation projects of industries, research institutes, and universities.
❍ Hanyang University is expanding into the world
Hanyang University, which strives for internationalization of universities in various ways, has
partnership with 697 universities in globe. Each year, more than 10,000 foreign and exchange
students, including undergraduate and graduate schools, pursue their study at Hanyang.
